name: IEC common-output element
summary: Element with a double top line that produces one output depending on all elements of an array above it.
description: TI's public overview of IEEE Std 91 describes the common-output element as having a double line at its top. It sits beneath an array of identical elements and produces a single output that depends on all of them, such as a combined carry or an all-equal flag. It must carry its own general qualifier to say what function it performs.

On data-book style drawings the common-output element saves repeating a gate for every bit. When reading it, look at the qualifier in the element (for example & or ≥1) and remember that its inputs come from each element above as well as any external inputs drawn on its side.
The double line only signals the structural role. Without the qualifier inside, the function is undefined, and the drawing should not be accepted in that state.
readingNotes: Look for the qualifier inside the double-line element; it defines the function.
Inputs come from every element in the array above.
drawingChecklist: Draw the double line clearly at the top of the element.
Show any additional external inputs on the side.
distinction: The common-control block has a notched outline at the top of an array and distributes inputs downwards; the common-output element collects results at the bottom.
